$comment: The ONLY place where a tier becomes a model name, and the only source of truth about the roster: which agents exist, what role each one plays, which tier it runs on and whether a human can pick it in the agent list. Every other file (AGENTS.md, .github/agents/*.agent.md, docs) refers to tiers and roles and is checked against this file by `npm run ai:validate`. A model name written anywhere else is a defect. Prices are deliberately absent: they are read from the pricing page when a decision needs them, because a copied number rots silently.

Kimi K3.note: open-weight model hosted by GitHub; off by default on Business and Enterprise plans — an administrator enables its policy before anyone can pick it

Kimi K2.7 Code.note: open-weight model hosted by GitHub; off by default on Business and Enterprise plans — an administrator enables its policy before anyone can pick it

policy.$comment: What the organisation's Copilot plan actually exposes in the model picker. Adjust this list first; then `tiers` — never the agent files. Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol were removed on 2026-09-14 by decision (cost). On 2026-09-15 the list was narrowed to one model per family — GPT-5.6 Luna (openai), Kimi K2.7 Code (moonshot), Claude Sonnet 5 (anthropic), Gemini 3.8 Flash (google) — plus GPT-5 mini, kept only because it is the one model this registry vouches for as a screenshot reader (vision tier). A tier cannot point at a model that is not listed here (A2).

tiers.$comment: Every tier runs the cheapest model that the policy exposes for its class ON PURPOSE: the agent files are procedures with exact commands and fixed return templates, the SDD tables are edited by scripts (npm run sdd), routing, the review draw and review merging are scripts, and review is cross-checked by several model families — a weak model has nothing to improvise. fast — mechanics (classification, tooling, unit tests, gates, commits) and the orchestrator. base — code, e2e, specs and prose review; since 2026-09-15 the same model as fast (GPT-5.6 Luna is the cheapest model in the picker, list price 2026-09-15: $0.20 in / $1.20 out per 1M tokens, against $0.75 / $4.50 for GPT-5.4 mini it replaced) — a second attempt after a red gate still costs less than one attempt on the dearer model; if base starts hitting the two-attempt STOP too often, the one edit is `base` → `Claude Sonnet 5`. main-<family> — the code-review seats (see `review`), named after the model family behind them; each takes the ONE model the policy exposes for that family (anthropic: Claude Sonnet 5, $2 / $10 — the only seat that is not the cheapest of its family, by decision of 2026-09-15). vision — a model that reads screenshots. Stronger models are one edit here (A2 requires them in policy.enabled).

agents.$comment: Names are `<domain>-<subject>`: `code-*` touches code, `doc-*` touches prose, `scm-*` touches git history, `mcp-*` talks to MCP servers; the one visible coordinator is plain `orchestrator` — there is exactly one, so it carries no subject. The role carries the permissions ai:validate enforces on the `tools:` list of each agent file. Exactly one agent is visible to a human — the orchestrator; everything else is reached through delegation.
agents.$commentForbidden: Tool sets no agent may list, whatever its role: data from outside the repository comes in through the scripts (alm:read, browser-inspector) and the MCP gateway, never through a browsing tool in a coding agent.

review.$comment: Code review is a cross-verification by several model families, not one reading. `seats` is the POOL: every seat gets the SAME brief and the SAME full scope (architecture, quality, security) and differs only in the family of the model behind it, so a finding two families agree on is confirmed and one vendor's blind spot cannot swallow the whole review. Each seat is named after the family it promises — `seats` maps the agent to that family — and `ai:validate` (A18) checks the promise: the model behind the seat's tier IS of that family, and no two seats share one. `seatsPerReview` says how many seats ONE review uses: `npm run review:draw` draws them at random from the pool (registry order kept) and records the draw in draw.json next to the reports, and `review:merge` reads that file as the list of families that owe a report — so a review costs `seatsPerReview` readings whatever the pool size, and the vendor mix rotates between reviews; equal to the pool size means every seat every time. A20 keeps the number between 2 (one reading is no cross-check) and the pool size. Swapping a vendor means renaming the seat, its tier and this entry, all under the gate; adding one is one more seat here. The orchestrator sends the brief in parallel, no seat sees another's report, and merges the tables with a count of agreeing families; the verdict is the worst of the seats.

mcp.$comment: Every MCP server declared in .vscode/mcp.json has exactly one owner — the integration subagent — and no other agent may name a server or one of its tools in `tools:`. The main session therefore never carries MCP tool schemas; the owner returns an artefact path plus a summary within the token budget.

ui.$comment: UI conventions as data. Mobile-first means: only min-width media queries, and every screen checked at all listed widths — the five widths code-reviewer-ui and the e2e tests go through.
